verdict.reasoning: Patient reports pain on urination for a few days: 'it's kind of a. Hurting when I. When I use the bathroom, when I pee, and it's been going on for a few days' and later summarized as 'the last three days you've been having a bit of burning pain on passing urine.'

Lower abdominal pain with voiding that is crampy and non-radiating is described: 'maybe sometimes get some like, pain kind of lowered down in my tummy when I go to the bathroom' and 'maybe sort of. Sort of cramping... But it's not like cramping like when I get. When I have a period or something.' She also denies radiation: 'Does the pain move anywhere else?... No, not really.'
She reports a small amount of blood in urine earlier today: 'There was a little bit of blood earlier today, but besides that? Not at all?'
Malodorous urine is reported: 'It does kind of. It kind of like doesn't smell very. Smells a bit weird, I guess.'

She denies frequency, nausea/vomiting, fever, and back/flank pain: 'Have you found yourself going to the toilet more often than normal?... I don't think so.'; 'With the symptoms, have you noticed any other symptoms, like nausea, vomiting? Doctor: No, not at all.'; 'Any fevers or temperatures?... No fever.'; 'Does the pain move anywhere else? Does it move towards the back or towards your flank, the sides? Doctor: No, not really.'
Bowel movements normal without diarrhea: 'in terms of your bowel, are your bowels working okay? Doctor: I think so, yeah.' and 'Any diarrhea, loose stool? Doctor: No, not that I've noticed at all.'

She is sexually active with a regular partner and uses condoms: 'are you currently sexually active? Yeah, I am with a regular partner.' and 'Do you use any form of contraception at all? Doctor: Yeah, we use condoms.'
No vaginal discharge: 'Have you noticed any other discharge from down below? Doctor: I haven't noticed anything, no. Patient: No.'
No prior STI screen: 'when was your last STD screen? If ever? Doctor: Don't think I've ever. I don't think I've ever had one.'
LMP a couple weeks ago and pregnancy considered unlikely: 'And when was your last period? Doctor: A couple weeks ago.' and 'Any chance you could be pregnant? ... Doctor: I don't think so.'
'So in the past I've had some. Some ibs, but other than that I think no. Like, no serious medical problems.' This supports a history of irritable bowel syndrome.
No regular medications: 'Do you take any regular medications? Doctor: No, I did a little bit ago or a couple days ago. Try some over the counter bicarbonate...' indicating no ongoing regular meds.
OTC bicarbonate tried without relief: 'I did a little bit ago or a couple days ago. Try some over the counter bicarbonate to try and help with the pain, but it wasn't really helping.'
Clindamycin allergy with swelling: 'Yeah, I'm allergic to clindamycin.' and 'What happens when you take clindamycin? Doctor: I get some like a swelling, basically.'
No relevant family history: 'is there anything I should be aware of related to kidneys, bladder, bowels, gut? Doctor: No, I don't think so. Not that I. Not anything I know about.'
Living situation and studies: 'So I live in a. Live in a flat near my college with a couple like friends of mine.' and 'I'm a student.'; 'I'm studying biology.'
Non-smoker: 'Do you smoke or do you drink much away of alcohol? Doctor: I don't. I don't smoke.'
Social alcohol use: 'I do drink, like on the weekends, socially.'

Assessment of simple cystitis with listed features matches transcript: 'Probably do have what we call a simple UTI or a urinary tract infection. Bladder'; dysuria, lower tummy cramps, malodorous urine, 'There was a little bit of blood earlier today', 'No fever', and 'Does the pain move anywhere else?... No' (no flank pain) are all documented.

Antibiotic choice and dosing: 'I'll give you a course of antibiotics today, something called either nitroferentoin or trimethoprine. And it's normally a three day course, so one tablet twice a day for three days.'
Hydration advice: 'I also advise you to drink plenty of fluids. Let's try and flush that, you know, that infection out your body.'
Cranberry juice suggestion: 'You can try cranberry juice. That can sometimes help with your symptoms.'

Sexual activity advice: 'if you can try and avoid it, I think that'd be sensible... Recommend you to continue using barrier contraception, but if you can avoid it while your symptoms clear up, that'll probably be the best for you and your boyfriend.'

The transcript only advises a pregnancy test if she is worried or as a general recommendation, not specifically as a plan if symptoms persist: 'if you are worried about the pain not getting any better, then I always advise you doing a pregnancy test to rule out pregnancy.' There is no statement 'If symptoms persist, a pregnancy test will be performed.'

Follow-up instructions: 'if you're still not better by the end of this week, I want you to give me a call or come back and see me' and 'things to look out for would be... high temperatures, back pain, just generally feeling more unwell. I do want to give you a call back.'
